findings.issue: AC-2 and AC-3 require HTTP 400 responses with specific machine-readable codes (`name_length`, `invalid_timezone`), but the existing `GlobalErrorHandler` returns `{message, code: null}` for bean-validation errors (`WebExchangeBindException`). The current error pipeline cannot satisfy these ACs without either (a) a custom validation exception handler that maps annotation names → codes, or (b) doing the validation in the service layer and throwing `AppException.badRequest(msg, code)` instead of relying on `@Size`/`@ValidTimezone`. The existing pattern in `auth/AuthService.java` and `profile/ProfileService.java` mixes both — but the spec doesn't say which is intended.
findings.why_matters: An implementer following AC-2/AC-3 literally will discover at integration-test time that bean-validation strips the code. They will then either weaken the AC (silently — bad), or rebuild the error path mid-implementation (slow, scope creep). The QA `curl` step in the AVP also asserts on the code field — those calls will fail unless this is resolved up front.
findings.fix: Either (a) drop the `code` requirement on AC-2/AC-3 and accept `{message: ..., code: null}` for bean-validation errors (matches existing profile/auth conventions); or (b) explicitly state in the spec that name-length and timezone validation MUST be implemented as service-layer pre-checks throwing `AppException.badRequest(msg, code)` (and remove the bean-validation annotations for those two fields, or accept a duplicate-validation cost). Pick one and write it into Технические решения. Recommend (a) — it matches `errors.profile.*` and `errors.auth.*` shape today.

findings.issue: Auto-suffix " (restored)" on name conflict during restore is silent — AC-14 only says the server appends the suffix "before save". There is no AC requiring the frontend to surface this rename to the user. The user could legitimately not notice that their restored project is now named differently, leading to confusion in audit-log review or in selector UI ("why is there an Acme and an Acme (restored)? when did I rename one?").
findings.why_matters: Silent server-side renames violate the principle of least surprise. With a 7-day grace window, the restore-with-conflict scenario is not a corner case — it can easily happen if a user soft-deletes Acme on Monday and creates a new Acme on Tuesday. By Sunday's restore, the suffix kicks in silently. This is a UX hole, not a security issue, but it is a credibility problem.
findings.fix: Add an explicit AC: when restore appends " (restored)", the response body carries the (new) suffixed name AND the frontend MUST show an informational toast (e.g. `errors.projects.restore.renamedDueToConflict`) explaining "Project was restored as 'X (restored)' because the name conflicted with an active project." Add the i18n key explicitly to the AC-25 list. Alternative: prompt the user before restore when a conflict is detected — heavier UX but no surprise.

findings.issue: The hard-delete cron job has no observability for the no-op case. AC-17 only requires `project_hard_deleted` events to be emitted PER deleted project. If the cron runs and finds zero soft-deleted-past-grace projects (the common case in early production), there is no audit trail that the job ran at all. Operations cannot distinguish "job is running daily but no work to do" from "job is silently broken".
findings.why_matters: JobRunr dashboard shows last-run timestamps, but this depends on the dashboard being reachable. For a daily cleanup job that handles GDPR-style data deletion, you want a structured log line at INFO level on every run with the count of deletions (zero or otherwise). Without it, the only way to verify the job is alive is to seed a test soft-delete and wait 7 days. This is a low-cost addition that pays for itself the first time a cron silently breaks.
findings.fix: Add to AC-17: `the cron emits a structured log entry per run with the number of projects hard-deleted (including 0)`, e.g. `log.info("hard-delete-projects: deleted {} projects, {} events", projectCount, eventCount)`. Mirror the existing `HardDeleteJob` (users) log pattern. Optionally (lower priority): emit a single `project_hard_delete_run` event per cron execution with metadata `{count, runAt}` — but logs are sufficient.

findings.issue: AC-24 (404 interceptor) is scoped to `/api/v1/projects/{currentProjectId}/*` — but TODAY no such child paths exist. The only project-scoped endpoints are the projects module's own (`/api/v1/projects/{id}`, `/api/v1/projects/{id}/restore`). The interceptor will never fire on the current codebase. It is forward-looking infrastructure for child epics. The spec doesn't acknowledge this — an implementer reading AC-24 might design a complex test suite for a code path that has zero current consumers.
findings.why_matters: Two risks: (1) testing AC-24 today requires fabricating a child endpoint or simulating a 404 from a non-existent path — the test could end up testing the interceptor's regex, not its behavior; (2) the interceptor catches 404s on any path matching the pattern, including `/api/v1/projects/{id}` itself (the GET single-resource endpoint), which legitimately returns 404 for soft-deleted/foreign IDs. This is the desired behavior (it triggers store reset on stale currentProjectId), but the spec doesn't disambiguate "404 from `GET /api/v1/projects/{currentProjectId}` (currently the only consumer)" vs "future 404 from `/api/v1/projects/{currentProjectId}/bots`".
findings.fix: Refine AC-24 to: "404 interceptor activates on any URL matching `/api/v1/projects/{currentProjectId}` OR `/api/v1/projects/{currentProjectId}/*`. Today only the former path exists; the wildcard is reserved for child-epic endpoints. Test today MUST cover: (a) GET `/api/v1/projects/{stale-id}` returning 404 triggers reset; (b) any other 404 (e.g. `/api/v1/projects` list with malformed query) does NOT trigger reset." Also add: "the interceptor must NOT trigger on 404s from non-projects URLs (`/api/profile`, `/api/auth`, future routes)."

findings.issue: Pinia store is in-memory only on MVP, with auto-select of most-recently-created project on each fresh session. The PRIMARY use-case in 'Зачем' is multi-brand business owners who actively work in multiple projects. For that exact persona, every browser restart will land them on whichever project they created last (likely the seasonal one, the test one, or the just-spun-up one) — NOT the one they spend most of their time in. The cost of localStorage with proper SSR gating (`import.meta.client`) is ~5 lines; the cost of auto-select-newest-on-each-session is a daily UX paper cut for the headline persona.
findings.why_matters: The interview record (Q-localstorage-rework) framed localStorage as 'over-engineered cross-tab sync'. But cross-tab sync was the OVER-engineered piece; cross-RESTART persistence (single tab, browser closed, reopened) is the load-bearing requirement that the workflow doc captured. Dropping localStorage drops both — and only the second was problematic. The trade-off framing in the interview was 'all-or-nothing' but the actual options were three: (a) full cross-tab + cross-restart, (b) cross-restart only, (c) nothing. The spec landed on (c) but (b) was the right answer.
findings.fix: Reconsider option (b) from the interview: localStorage write on selectProject(), localStorage read on store init, gated by `if (import.meta.client)`. No `storage` event listener, no Pinia plugin, no cross-tab sync. SSR-safe by gating, no fragility from cross-tab events. Total surface: ~5 lines in the store + 1 helper for safe localStorage access. If the team holds at (c), at minimum add an AC mandating that the auto-select decision is announced in a toast so users aren't confused why their selector switched.

findings.issue: The `(ownerId, name)` uniqueness pre-check race window is described as 'microseconds, acceptable at the limit of 5'. This understates the actual window. Service-layer pre-check + insert is a Mongo round-trip pair: under typical replica-set latency (5-30ms primary read, 5-30ms primary write), the race window is ~10-60ms per operation pair, not microseconds. The 'limit of 5' argument carries the safety, not the timing.
findings.why_matters: The framing is accurate in conclusion (the race is vanishingly rare) but inaccurate in mechanism. A reviewer who flags timing might disagree based on real Mongo numbers. The spec's defense should hold up to that scrutiny.
findings.fix: Reword Risk #3 mitigation: 'race window dominated by Mongo primary round-trip (~10-60ms in production replica sets); collision odds remain vanishingly rare given the 5-project per-user quota and single-owner concurrency profile (a user does not race against themselves at scale). If a real production incident surfaces, fall back to programmatic `IndexOps.ensureIndex` with `partialFilterExpression`.'

findings.issue: AC-25 requires i18n parity for `projects.*`, `errors.projects.*`, `layout.*`, `validation.*` namespaces but does not enumerate the actual key surface. The locale-parity build gate enforces 'same keys in both files', not 'all required keys present'. A spec gap (e.g. forgetting `errors.projects.restore.renamedDueToConflict` in AC-14, or `projects.delete.confirmTypeName` for the typing-confirmation modal) will pass the parity gate by being absent from BOTH files.
findings.why_matters: i18n bugs caused by missing keys silently fall back to the key path string in production (Vue I18n behavior). The `useApiError` composable gates with `te()` so it falls back to `errors.generic`, but UI strings (selector, settings, danger zone) do not have that fallback. Risk: a user-facing label renders as `projects.delete.danger.confirmButton` literally.
findings.fix: Add an enumerated key list to a 'Технические решения' bullet (or to AC-25 itself): minimum `projects.{create,settings,delete,restore,deleted,empty}.*`, `errors.projects.{create,update,delete,restore}.{400,401,404,409,422,generic}`, `layout.{projectSelector,createFirstProject}`, `validation.{projectName,timezone}*`. Tech-spec can finalize the exact set; user-spec just needs to commit to the surface so QA can grep for missing keys before merge.

findings.issue: Manual AVP step 10 ('open /jobrunr-dashboard, confirm hard-delete-projects is registered') is ceremony, not regression coverage. The integration test that exercises the cron via direct method invocation already proves the bean wires up. Recurring-job registration is asserted at startup-time (JobRunr fails fast if the @Recurring annotation can't parse). A human eyeball check is fragile, slow, and adds nothing the unit/integration test layer doesn't already provide.
findings.why_matters: The AVP runs on every deploy. A manual checklist item per deploy adds friction without value. Worse, the dashboard route depends on infrastructure (the dashboard is enabled in dev, may be disabled in prod via security rules — that decision is outside this epic's scope). If prod doesn't expose the dashboard, this AVP step becomes impossible to satisfy.
findings.fix: Reframe AVP step 10 as: 'one-time post-deploy verification (NOT per-deploy regression). Skip if the JobRunr dashboard is not exposed in the target environment.' Better: replace with an integration-test assertion that `BackgroundJobServer.getRecurringJobs()` contains the entry — which makes it a per-deploy gate via the existing test pipeline, no manual step needed.

findings.issue: The 'Технические решения' section names specific implementation entities: `ProjectService.requireOwned(ownerId, id)`, `frontend/stores/projects.ts`, `AppException.notFound(...)`, `@ValidTimezone` annotation, `WithMockAppUser` test utility relocation. These are tech-spec territory (HOW), not user-spec (WHAT/WHY).
findings.why_matters: User-spec is the contract with the product; tech-spec is the contract with the implementation. Mixing them makes the user-spec brittle (a method rename in implementation now requires a user-spec update) and gives the tech-spec author less room to choose the best approach. The interview justifications for these decisions are sound — they belong in the tech-spec's 'Decisions' section with rationale, NOT in the user-spec.
findings.fix: Move method/file/class names from 'Технические решения' to tech-spec. Keep the user-spec at the level of: 'access guard reusable across modules' (not `requireOwned(ownerId, id)`), 'frontend store for project state' (not `stores/projects.ts`), 'strict IANA timezone validation' (not `@ValidTimezone` + `getAvailableZoneIds().contains`). The current section is mostly fine but the surface-level entity names should go. Note: this is form-only — none of the decisions themselves are wrong.

findings.issue: Workflow original AC #5 is 'Перемикач проектів працює і запам'ятовує останній обраний' (selector remembers last selected). The user-spec consciously deviates to 'auto-select most-recently-created on each fresh session'. The deviation is documented in scope and acknowledged in interview Q-localstorage-rework, but workflow AC #5 is technically NOT met as written — only a weakened version is.
findings.why_matters: The workflow doc is the source-of-truth for MVP scope. Conscious deviations are acceptable when justified, but they should be enumerated explicitly in a 'Conscious deviations from workflow doc' section so future readers (and the next epic) know why this AC says X and the workflow says Y. Currently the deviation is mentioned in passing in 'Ограничения' bullet 6 and 'Сценарій 2' but not consolidated.
findings.fix: Add a short 'Conscious deviations from workflow doc' subsection (or expand 'Ограничения') listing: (1) workflow says 403, spec says 404 (anti-enumeration); (2) workflow says full-page onboarding, spec says inline empty-state on /dashboard; (3) workflow says localStorage persistence of last-selected, spec says in-memory + auto-select-newest. Reference workflow line numbers. AC-31 already requires updating ux-guidelines.md to match — extend the bullet to cover the workflow-doc deviation tracker too. (Alternative: leave as-is and accept that workflow doc is a guideline, not a hard contract — but make that policy explicit somewhere in project-knowledge.)

summary: Spec is well-researched and right-sized for L; the team has made defensible choices throughout. Two blocking issues: AC-2/AC-3 demand response codes that the current error pipeline doesn't emit (fixable by either weakening the AC or moving validation to service layer), and the silent restore-suffix UX needs an explicit user-facing toast. Recommend resolving the AC-2/AC-3 code-field ambiguity before tech-spec to avoid mid-implementation rework.
